What you can print on a bubble mailer

A padded mailer has one large flat panel on the front and another on the back, and both print cleanly. Most brands put a logo and a short line of text on the front, a return-address panel on the back, and leave the rest of the mailer plain so the courier label has room. Full-bleed color, patterns and inside-flap messages are all possible; they cost more because they use more ink and need tighter registration.

  • One color: a logo and a web address in a single spot color. The lowest-cost option and the one most small brands start with.
  • Two colors: a logo in brand color plus a second color for text or a return panel.
  • Full color: CMYK print for photographic artwork, gradients or busy patterns. Best on white poly.
  • Both sides: front branding plus a printed back, often used for care instructions or a reorder prompt.

If you are deciding between finishes first, our kraft bubble mailers page shows the ten numbered sizes the natural stock comes in.

Custom bubble mailer pricing by quantity

Printing is priced per unit on top of the plain mailer, and the per-unit figure falls as the run grows because plate and setup costs are fixed. The table shows an indicative ladder for a 7x9 kraft mailer with a one-color logo, taken from the same rates the Design Your Bubble Mailer section on each product page uses. Larger sizes, more colors and specialty stocks move the figures up; the written quote is the firm number.

A useful rule: if you ship more than 300 orders a month, printing at 2,500 or 5,000 units almost always beats reordering 500 at a time, even after storage.

Artwork, proofing and lead time

Send vector artwork (PDF, AI or EPS) with text outlined, or a 300 dpi raster file at print size if that is all you have. Name spot colors as Pantone references. We place the artwork on a template of the exact mailer size and send a digital proof; you approve it by email before anything prints, and revisions before approval are free.

Plain stock leaves within a few business days. Printed runs are made to order, so allow a few weeks after proof approval as a planning figure, longer for full-color or custom sizes; an express production add-on is available when a launch date is fixed. We confirm the lead time on your quote so you can plan the launch around it.

Which stock prints best

Kraft: natural brown paper face, best with dark one- or two-color logos; inks warm slightly on the stock.
White poly: smooth, water-resistant, the truest color reproduction and the right base for full-color print.
Metallic: reflective film for a retail-facing look; one-color print only.
Recyclable paper: curbside-recyclable paper padding with a kraft face; prints like kraft.
Custom sizes: any stock, quoted on request when none of the eleven standard sizes fits.

FAQ

Custom printed bubble mailer FAQs

Printed runs are quoted from 250 units, the lowest quantity in Design Your Bubble Mailer. Most brands print 1,000 or more because the plate and setup cost is spread across the run and the per-unit price drops sharply between 500 and 2,500.

As a guide, a 7x9 kraft mailer with a one-color logo works out around $0.43 each at 1,000 units and about $0.29 at 10,000, before shipping. Size, material, number of colors and quantity all move the figure. The Design Your Bubble Mailer section on any product page gives an instant range; the emailed quote is firm.

One and two spot colors are the standard for logos and return panels. Full-color (CMYK) print is available for photographic or gradient artwork, and we can print both sides. Pantone references are matched as closely as the stock allows; white poly gives the truest color, kraft warms every ink slightly.

Vector files (PDF, AI or EPS) with text outlined are best. If you only have a PNG or JPG, send it at 300 dpi or higher at print size and we will tell you whether it is usable. Spot colors should be named as Pantone references; CMYK is fine for full-color work.

Yes. Every custom order gets a digital proof showing the artwork positioned on the actual mailer size. Nothing prints until you approve it by email, and revisions before approval are free.

Plain stock ships in a few business days. Because printed mailers are made to order, the lead time depends on quantity and the number of colors; as a planning figure allow a few weeks after proof approval. Express production is available as an add-on when a launch date is fixed, and we confirm the exact lead time on your quote.

Both. Kraft takes dark one- and two-color print well and gives a natural, recycled look. White poly is the better base for light colors, fine detail and full-color print. Metallic and recyclable paper stocks can also be printed.

Yes. If none of the eleven stock sizes fits, give us the packed dimensions of your product and we will quote a custom size. Custom sizes carry a higher minimum than printed stock sizes; we confirm it on the quote.

No. Delivery of your order is free anywhere in the USA, printed or plain. And once you are shipping with them, printing adds nothing to the weight, so postage is the same as a plain mailer of that size.

For pallet-quantity programs, yes. Many brands print 10,000 or 25,000 at the lower unit price and take scheduled releases so they are not holding a full pallet in a small warehouse. Ask about release schedules when you request your quote.
